domain: Theology / Religious Studies / History of Christianity
topic_summary: Analysis of Christian scriptural authority frameworks, examining how different traditions ground interpretive legitimacy in the biblical text. The Protestant Reformation crystallized two fundamental readings of the same canonical substrate: sola scriptura (scripture alone as sufficient authority) versus scripture-plus-tradition (scripture interpreted through magisterial continuity). These readings instantiate structurally different constraints on ecclesiastical power, sacramental validity, and doctrinal development.

key_entities: Christian Bible (canonical text, Old + New Testament)
Individual believer (Protestant locus of interpretive authority)
key_tensions: Direct textual access vs mediated interpretation (individual reader vs institutional authority)
Textual sufficiency vs tradition necessity (sola scriptura vs scripture-plus-tradition)
key_mechanisms: Vernacular translation (enables direct access, reduces clerical gatekeeping)
Sola fide justification (removes sacramental mediation requirement)

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: Christian Bible as canonical text grounding legitimate doctrine and practice
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Contested: Protestant traditions ground authority in scripture-alone with individual/congregational interpretation; Catholic/Orthodox traditions ground authority in scripture-interpreted-through-tradition with magisterial/conciliar interpretation
commitment_system_recognition.candidate_pattern: Legitimation Monopoly — interpretive authority structures control which readings count as legitimate; Protestant fragmentation vs Catholic centralization represent different drift-absorption strategies

readings.commitment: Scripture alone is sufficient and self-interpreting authority for doctrine and practice
readings.authority_grounding: Direct textual access; priesthood of all believers; Holy Spirit illumination for individual readers
readings.expected_structural_delta: Low clerical extraction (congregational autonomy); high doctrinal fragmentation (no adjudicative monopoly); sacraments as ordinances not salvific channels; beneficiary is lay believer autonomy; victim is doctrinal coherence across communities

readings.commitment: Scripture requires tradition for authoritative interpretation; magisterium guards deposit of faith
readings.authority_grounding: Apostolic succession; papal/episcopal teaching authority; continuity with early church fathers
readings.expected_structural_delta: High clerical extraction (sacramental mediation required); low doctrinal fragmentation (centralized adjudication); sacraments as grace-conferring; beneficiary is institutional hierarchy; victim is lay interpretive agency

readings.commitment: Scripture interpreted through ecumenical councils and patristic consensus; tradition as living continuity not magisterial decree
readings.authority_grounding: Conciliar authority (councils not popes); symphonia of tradition; patristic exegesis as normative
readings.expected_structural_delta: Moderate clerical extraction (episcopal not papal); moderate fragmentation (autocephalous churches); sacraments as mysteries; beneficiary is episcopal collegiality; victim is rapid doctrinal adaptation

axiom_contradictions.basis: Sola scriptura's axiom (text is self-sufficient for doctrine) requires rejecting tradition-scripture's axiom (text requires authoritative tradition for correct interpretation). No single framework can hold both scripture-sufficiency and tradition-necessity simultaneously.

Sola scriptura rejects binding authority of post-apostolic tradition; conciliar reading treats ecumenical councils and patristic consensus as authoritative interpretive tradition. These are mutually exclusive claims about whether tradition binds interpretation.

axes.structural_delta: Scripture as sole sufficient authority; individual/congregational interpretation without required institutional mediation
axes.primary_observable: Presence/absence of extra-biblical tradition in doctrinal statements; congregational vs hierarchical polity structures; vernacular Bible distribution rates
axes.selection_reason: Primary reading instantiating Protestant constraint structure; high epsilon due to elimination of sacramental extraction; establishes baseline for comparison

axes.structural_delta: Scripture requires authoritative tradition; magisterial interpretation as necessary channel for legitimate doctrine
axes.primary_observable: Papal/episcopal teaching authority in practice; sacramental requirement for salvation; extra-biblical tradition (Marian dogma, purgatory) in official doctrine
axes.selection_reason: Structurally opposed reading; same observable domain (interpretive authority) but inverted beneficiary/victim structure; axiom-contradictory to sola_scriptura_reading

axes.human_readable: Conciliar Reading (Episcopal Consensus Without Papal Monarchy)
axes.structural_delta: Scripture interpreted through councils and patristic tradition; episcopal collegiality without papal supremacy
axes.primary_observable: Conciliar decision-making vs papal decree; autocephalous church structures; weight given to church fathers vs recent magisterial teaching
axes.selection_reason: Third structurally distinct position; splits difference between Protestant and Catholic on extraction axis; demonstrates that kernel admits more than binary opposition; completes triadic topology

omegas.description: All three readings treat the canon (which books count as Scripture) as settled, but canon formation itself required extra-biblical tradition (councils of Hippo/Carthage). This creates a bootstrap problem for sola scriptura: using tradition to establish the text that renders tradition unnecessary. Sola scriptura reading may be internally unstable on this dimension.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 2 (Absence Inventory): canon-selection mechanism absent from extraction

omegas.description: Does the Protestant reading instantiate a genuine alternative constraint or a secularization pathway that ultimately dissolves scriptural authority itself? 500 years of fragmentation (30,000+ denominations) may indicate that removing institutional adjudication creates runaway interpretive drift, collapsing the constraint entirely. If true, sola_scriptura is not a stable reading but a transition state.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan): lay autonomy as beneficiary may be instrumental cover for dissolution of shared constraint

omegas.description: Analysis assumes Western Reformation/Counter-Reformation binary. African, Asian, Latin American Christianity may instantiate readings not reducible to this topology (e.g., Pentecostal Spirit-authority, liberation theology praxis-authority). These may be fourth/fifth readings of the same kernel or evidence that 'biblical authority' itself is a Western framing.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 1 (Operational Medium): analysis operates within Western denominational categories

omegas.description: Feminist and liberation theology readings challenge the kernel itself: if the text encodes patriarchal/colonial power, interpretive authority becomes a trap regardless of whether it is individual or institutional. These readings may argue for abandoning the kernel rather than selecting an interpretive framework.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 2 (Absence Inventory): critical hermeneutics absent from extraction

fracture_scan.notes: Clean scan. Three readings represent genuine structural alternatives with axiom contradictions. Canon formation bootstrap (omega_canon_formation) noted but does not invalidate reading structure. Deferred axes empty because kernel decomposition exhausts the structural space for this particular commitment system.
